name: rotating_vector
about: One attacker, one target, and a different vector every pulse: amplified DNS, then NTP, then SSDP, then memcached, then impossible TCP flags, then fragment abuse. The source keeps hitting its own counter slot throughout, so the evidence that justifies a refusal is continuous even though no single exception counter is. This is the shape a rented booter produces when it cycles its method list, and it is a trap for any detector that keys its state on the vector rather than on the source: six counters each rising for one pulse and flat for five look like six small incidents rather than one sustained attack. The ladder should read it as the latter - climbing once and holding across the rotation, not restarting at each change - and the reversals column is where that shows.

timeline.note: ten seconds of quiet after the last vector
